title: matplotlib: one figure, two subplots
source:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

days = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
milk_l = [21, 23, 22, 25, 24, 26, 27]
goats = {"Ada": 4.2, "Bo": 3.1, "Cy": 3.8}

fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.5))
left.plot(days, milk_l, marker="o")
left.set_title("Milk per day")
left.set_xlabel("Day")
left.set_ylabel("Litres")
right.bar(list(goats), list(goats.values()))
right.set_title("Milk per goat")
fig.suptitle("Dairy week")
plt.show()

steps.narration: days now refers to a new list.
milk_l now refers to a new list.
goats now refers to a new dict.
Made a new figure with 2 sets of axes (subplots) in 1 row of 2, 9 × 3.5 inches; it is now the current figure.
Drew a line plot of milk_l against days on left.
Set the title of left to "Milk per day".
Set the x-axis label of left to "Day".
Set the y-axis label of left to "Litres".
Drew a bar chart on right: one bar for each item of list(goats), its height from list(goats.values()).
Set the title of right to "Milk per goat".
Set the overall title of fig to "Dairy week".
Figure 1 is in the output, titled Dairy week. It has 2 subplots: (1) a line plot titled Milk per day, with the x axis labelled Day and the y axis Litres; (2) a bar chart titled Milk per goat.
